correctness.rationale: The exact one-F-class multinomial weight is s!/[j!ell!(s-j-ell)!] 2^{-r(j+ell)}(1-2^{1-r})^{s-j-ell}. With u=s2^{-r}, m u^h tending to lambda, and u r^d tending to zero for every fixed d, profiles of total rare monochromatic E-block number t<h have divergent outer-class counts, t>h disappear, and exactly h pure monochromatic blocks have independent Poisson counts with intensities lambda/[j!(h-j)!]. The finite-depth E/F/P back-and-forth truncation must distinguish near-monochromatic E-types with finitely many exceptions: at critical total h, any exception destroys criticality by the u*r^d hypothesis. This partitions q-types into abundant, vanishing and finitely many independent Poisson types; fixed FO sentence probabilities follow. E/P reduct has abundant finite color-type witnesses, but an F-definable h-blue-block event has limiting probability 1-exp(-lambda/h!), so alternating critical intensities genuinely prevent convergence in full language. A separate exact multinomial finite consistency check and verified source tree corroborate, not prove, the limit.
